findings.problem: Checkout returns 12 although the agreed total is 10.
findings.principle: Existing commitment: agreed checkout total is 10.
findings.consequence: Passing mocked tests conceal a failing local HTTP checkout.
findings.fix: Retain expected total 10. Resolve whether service data or core pricing policy produces it; then fix that owner and add matching public-interface protection.
findings.verification: Journey must return status 201,total 10 with agreed service data; unit expectations must come from design.

findings.problem: Web imports private storage directly and through a compiler alias.
findings.principle: Existing commitment: UI never touches storage; callers use public core interface.
findings.consequence: Storage changes leak into web; alias module also fails Node runtime resolution.
findings.fix: Keep transport/storage private; expose the minimum checkout-facing capability through core index; migrate web callers to public interface. Do not merely re-export raw storage. Replace private alias usage with public import.
findings.verification: Native boundary check must reject direct/aliased private imports and allow public import; Node public callers and checkout must execute.

findings.problem: Core a and b call each other without a terminating path.
findings.principle: Proposed: reachable core capabilities terminate; keep static dependency cycles out of core unless justified.
findings.consequence: Invoking either recurses indefinitely; existing boundary command fails even though checkout does not import them.
findings.fix: Review intended use before removing unused cycle or replacing recursion with the intended terminating behavior. Keep this separate from checkout pricing.
findings.verification: Boundary cycle diagnostic disappears; any retained public behavior has termination coverage.

findings.problem: The standard test/type commands pass despite journey and boundary failures.
findings.principle: Proposed: checkout acceptance and approved import boundary are required alongside unit/type checks.
findings.consequence: A contributor can report green tests while violating both approved commitments.
findings.fix: Add one local verification script chaining existing check,test,journey,boundaries with failure propagation; point AGENTS.md to DESIGN.md and this command. Preserve all individual commands; CI remains separately selected.
findings.verification: Aggregate exits nonzero for each failing component; all four pass on a repaired final state.

findings.problem: Price response and quantity are consumed without runtime validation.
findings.principle: Proposed: validate service data and checkout inputs before recording a purchase.
findings.consequence: Malformed service data or invalid quantity can produce invalid totals with status 201.
findings.fix: Agree valid quantity/price ranges and failure outcomes; validate at public core boundary, reject HTTP/payload errors before order mutation. Do not invent retry, timeout or currency policies.
findings.verification: Valid agreed inputs succeed; malformed JSON, missing/nonfinite price, non-success HTTP and invalid quantities yield agreed failures without recording orders.

findings.problem: Order has two conflicting glossary definitions.
findings.principle: Proposed: distinguish customer purchase from UI panel sequence in project vocabulary.
findings.consequence: Future purchase contracts may be confused with presentation order.
findings.fix: Review distinct terms such as Order and Panel sequence; edit existing glossary only after terminology selection; no naming migration.
findings.verification: Review confirms each term has one domain meaning and preserves approved checkout commitments.

limitations: Checks captured in checks.json manually; not through an approved run-checks plan and not bound to findings fingerprint. Readiness therefore unverified.
